text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian newspapers this morning.
- Leading Norwegian economists say they doubt interest rates will rise sharply. The experts recommend mortgage lenders not to fix loans at a specific rate but to let the rate float.
- Norwegians have paid 160 million crowns in fines so far this year. Around one third of the amount is a result of violated traffic rules.

- Police have started a computer register of people who own weapons without a permit. So far three out of 54 police districts have applied for permission to register personal data on those owning guns.
- Swedish authorities suspect that unemployed Swedish construction workers are working in Norway while still claiming state benefits at home.
- Signals in the paper market are positive. Vidar Lerstad, manager at forestry company Norske Skogindustrier, says he expects prices to rise.
- After a sharp rise in house prices estate agents can look forward to record results in 1997.
